chapter_title: Concerning the Catechumen who found fault with the Elect: why he is angry.
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly a situational pastoral/homiletic piece (catechumen vs. Elect), wrapped in narrative frame. The only recoverable older substrate is a small cluster of dualist-anthropological statements (divinity from the heights; alien body; the “two essences”) embedded inside exhortation and institutional categories (Elect/saints). No systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping sequence appears here; the correspondential tree image functions as moral application, not cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative opening with titles (“my master, the apostle”) and scene-setting; hagiographic/dialogue frame rather than teaching.
Speech of the catechumen within the dialogue setup; rhetorical complaint about ‘righteous ones’ and behavior, not cosmological exposition.
Dialogue attribution (“our enlightener speaks”)—a classic compiling-frame marker.
Exhortation plus an illustrative parable (scented-oil tree) used to correct behavior; correspondence is deployed to address community conduct (pointing), not to map the cosmic system (being).

paragraphs.core_text: They are gods as they stand firm in the image of the gods. The divinity that is planted in them came to them from the heights and [dw]elt in them. They have done the will of the greatness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/application hinge: “This is also the case with the elect.” It anchors the doctrinal claims to the church category ‘elect’ and functions as pastoral comparison, not substrate exposition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying cosmological anthropology (indwelling divinity from the heights; ‘image of the gods’) is plausibly older teaching, but it is embedded in an ecclesial comparison about the Elect.

paragraphs.core_text: You know, once and for all, they are established in a body that is not their own, hating the flesh of Sin that makes the other dwell in a foreign land.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the pastoral/emotional application and reassurance about anger/quarrelling (“Further, when they will be troubled…”, “However, do not you be troubled…”, and the concluding causal application to ‘hard words’). Kept only the anthropological mechanism (alien body; flesh of Sin; exile/foreign land).
paragraphs.temporal_note: This preserves a compact piece of dualist mechanism (alien embodiment; Sin as an agentive force), which stays within the Manichaean cosmic-anthropological system, though originally framed to justify the Elect’s behavior.

paragraphs.core_text: For you have known the mystery of the two essences, you have understood that what is good and what is evil dwell in every person.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the surrounding imperatives and the institutional/ethical application about how to treat ‘them/the saints’ (“do not…”, “do not ask…”, and the burden/saints material), retaining only the doctrinal statement of the ‘two essences’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A brief doctrinal kernel (two essences; mixed indwelling of good/evil) embedded in direct second-person admonition—likely an older teaching fragment used pastorally.

Direct accusation and moral instruction to the catechumen (sins, lifestyle), plus institutional teacher-disciple relations; ‘Cross of Light’ appears, but only as part of ethical reproach and community discipline.
Pure exhortation/application voice (“love and honour them… do not speak against them”) with no independent cosmological exposition.
Narrative transition and emotional response scene (“weeping”); part of dialogue frame/closure movement.
Catechumen’s penitential reply addressed to “my master,” reiterating lesson within the narrative container; not a systematic teaching layer, and includes late-style confessional posture.
